title: Democratization of Point-of-Care Viral Biosensors: Bridging the Gap from Academia to the Clinic
content: The COVID-19 pandemic and recent viral outbreaks have underscored the urgent need for diagnostics that combine accuracy with widespread accessibility. While laboratory-based methods remain essential, point-of-care (POC) solutions are critical for quick, decentralized testing. Significant advancements in viral biosensors, from innovative technologies to enhancements of existing platforms, demonstrate the growing potential of new sensing technologies for clinical applications. However, a gap remains between academic proof-of-concept studies and viable, clinically deployable diagnostic tools. This review examines how recent advancements in sensing methodologies, including innovative analyte detection, simplified assay administration, and enhanced performance in complex media such as serum, collectively address barriers to adoption, including cost, usability, and scalability. We also explore broader trends, such as open-source hardware, modular assay design, and standardized reporting practices, that collectively work to reduce barriers to clinical implementation. By analyzing these converging innovations, we emphasize how interdisciplinary progress is transforming the landscape of viral diagnostics, bringing the field closer to practical, equitable, and scalable solutions for real-world settings through novel biosensing advancements.
